page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor, providing 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 960.0 GB of system memory, yielding 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a combined 320 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and top-tier memory performance. The Intel Xeon processor achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 96,293.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 85,426.66, supported by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. Memory bandwidth is a notable highlight, with cached small-block read operations reaching 7,649.82 GB/sec and large-block reads at 316.04 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the system demonstrated top-tier LLM inference speeds on a small 135M model, processing 10,308.98 tokens/sec for prompts and generating 377.14 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a high ratio of memory and GPU acceleration per vCPU, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that saturate GPU and memory channels before CPU cores. However, a key tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation model and the complete absence of local storage, which requires careful architectural planning for I/O-heavy operations. The instance is engineered for large-scale artificial intelligence workloads, deep learning training, large language model inference, complex physical simulations, and memory-intensive database operations.
